human_tolerance.notes: Found in residential areas throughout its range and drawn to sunflower and safflower seed feeders; the male defends a territory vigorously and will fight its own reflection.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Judgement window. Wikipedia gives 'Two or three, and even four, broods are raised each year' and a 12-13 day incubation with fledging 10-11 days after hatching, but no calendar months; the window is placed over the spring and summer months in the southern part of the range.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Judgement window covering the rest of the year, when 'the male behaves territorially, marking out his territory with song' and pairs stay together.

vocalizations.description: A loud, clear whistle sung from the top of a tree or another high location by the male to defend his territory and keep other males out; females and pairs also sing, and the song is learned, so it varies regionally.
A distinctive short metallic chip, often given when predators approach the nest, warning the female and nestlings.

taxonomy.note: Linnaeus 1758, Cardinalis cardinalis; family Cardinalidae per the GBIF backbone and ITIS TSN 179124.

common_names.note: en/fr/es labels; the English name follows the Wikipedia article title, the fr/es labels the Wikidata sitelink titles.

range.note: Native list from the lead and distribution section: 'southeastern Canada, through the eastern United States from Maine to Minnesota to Texas, New Mexico, southern Arizona, southern California and south through Mexico, Belize, and Guatemala', plus an allopatric Pacific-slope population in Mexico. Introduced list from 'introduced to Bermuda in 1700. It has also been introduced in Hawaii.' Koppen classes are the author's judgement of the described range.

traits.limb_count.note: Biped: two legs, the forelimbs modified as wings.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'It is a ground feeder and finds food while hopping on the ground through trees or shrubbery', and it perches and flies; the walking and running a cardinal also does is folded into the block model's hop.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endotherm: a bird, active by day and roosting at night.

traits.skin.note: Feathers: plumage described in detail in the Description section.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight between perches, trees and feeders.

traits.metamorphosis.note: None: the young hatch as chicks and 'Newly hatched cardinals weigh an average of 3-3.5 grams, are naked, blind, and immobile'.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The female builds a cup nest in a well-concealed spot in dense shrub or a low tree 1-3 m off the ground', of twigs, bark strips and grasses.

traits.perching.note: Perches to sing: 'The male sings in a loud, clear whistle from the top of a tree or another high location'.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg: the validator bands a bird under 0.05 kg as Tiny and under 1 kg as Small, and 0.045 kg falls in the first band, so Tiny is the value that matches the mass. Wikipedia itself calls the bird 'mid-sized', a judgement about a songbird rather than a mass band.

traits.mass_kg.note: 'The adult weighs from 33.6-65 g, with an average 44.8 g.'

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 'a body length of 21-23.5 cm (8.3-9.3 in)'.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 'a wingspan of 25-31 cm (9.8-12.2 in)'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives no lifespan figure for this species, only 'Populations appear to remain stable or increasing' and a global population of some 100 million. Authored as a rough 3.2 years for a small songbird; not a sourced number.

traits.diet.note: 'The diet of the adult northern cardinal consists mainly (up to 90%) of weed seeds, grains, and fruits. It will also consume snails and insects'. The seed share uses the stated 90% plant figure reduced to allow for the insect and snail items the article lists; the seed/fruit/invertebrate split within those groups is the author's judgement, as the article does not separate them.

traits.social.note: 'Pairs generally stay together year-round but are not necessarily monogamous', and 'Mated pairs sometimes sing together before nesting'; group_size is a judgement of a pair plus any attending young and neighbours at a feeder.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Diurnal: a 'territorial song bird' singing and feeding by day.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the male 'will chase off other males entering his territory' and 'will fight its reflection relentlessly', which is threat display and displacement rather than physical defence, so Flee is the closest schema value.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, from a bird that is 'found in residential areas throughout its range' and comes to feeders (low wariness) but keeps a well-concealed nest and flees from an intruder (higher than the house sparrow).

habitat.use.note: 'Its natural habitat is in woodlands, gardens, shrublands, and wetlands', and it is 'most abundant ... in areas where dense cover is interspersed with open areas, such as woodland edges, brushy fields, wooded wetlands, parks, and suburban areas'. Most foraging is on the ground, with the rest in shrubs and low trees; the split is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Nests and shelters in 'dense shrub or a low tree', in thick shrubs, trees and vine tangles.

habitat.resources.note: Seed, invertebrate and fruit weights follow the stated diet shares; the two shrub_thicket entries are for nesting and general cover, and perch for the song perch, all from the habitat and nesting sections.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity and uses_gardens from 'The northern cardinal is found in residential areas throughout its range. Bird feeders attract it' and from the increase in range 'An increase in backyard feeding by humans has increased the range of this species'; light_max, flight_distance_m and road_mortality are judgement values, the article giving no figures.

seasonal.strategy.note: Resident: the range description has no migration, the bird is 'found in residential areas throughout its range' and pairs 'stay together year-round'.

seasonal.phases.note: Wikipedia gives brood counts ('Two or three, and even four, broods are raised each year') and a 12-13 day incubation with fledging 10-11 days after hatching, but no calendar months at all. Both phase windows are the author's judgement, placed over the spring and summer breeding months in the southern part of the range and the rest of the year for territorial song.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Incubation takes 12 or 13 days. Young fledge 10 or 11 days after hatching.' duration_days is the sum of those two spans as an approximation, and scale is a judgement of a partly grown fledgling.

look.note: Male plumage from the Description section: 'a mid-sized perching songbird with a body length of 21-23.5 cm and a crest on the top of its head ... males are a vibrant red color, and have a black mask on the face, as well as a larger crest', with 'the distinctive red-orange beak'. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement: the crest part carries the crest and the mask part the black face mask.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: seed-led ground foraging, an early (February-August) nest-building window for a multi-brood season, a longer song cooldown for a loud territorial whistle, and a short flee distance for a bird that watches people closely from cover.
